title: Private or public?
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Who do you answer to every three months?

Jose asked: why does he want to take it private? A student said: as a general comment, one of the advantages of going private is that executives at public companies talk about having to manage to the street, making short-term decisions at the expense of long-term ones so as not to miss quarterly goals and take a hit on the stock price.

The student said: the argument is that when you are private you are not worried about running quarter to quarter. You are running year to year and five-year plans, and it allows better strategic decisions, even if they have a short-term impact.
It is amazing, Jose said, the way a whole company culture changes, and I've seen it when companies go private and then public, where the focus becomes: what is our stock price?

A famous investor doesn't worry about the stock price, he said. He worries about the fundamentals of the business and the long-term strategy. Being a public company can be very distracting for a long-term view.
A student added: we all know he cuts a lot of expenses. Jose said: then he has to develop a business model so it can make money.
What would you do differently if nobody watched your numbers every quarter?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the short-term numbers you answer to.
Write the long-term decisions they push you away from.
Write what would change if you answered only yearly.
Write the fundamentals of your business.
Write what you would measure instead of the stock price or its equivalent.

check.q: What did a student say public executives must do?
choices: Manage to the street, with short-term decisions

check.q: What did Jose say changes when a company goes public?
choices: The whole culture: the focus becomes the stock price

check.q: What did Jose say a famous investor worries about?
choices: The fundamentals and the long-term strategy

recap: Notice the short-term pressure you answer to. Keep your eye on the fundamentals.
